title: Auto envvar applied to empty envvar
detail: The check uses `not envvar`, which is true for empty strings or empty lists. This causes an auto-generated envvar to be used even when the user explicitly set an empty envvar, violating the intended behaviour that an empty envvar should be treated as no envvar.
note: About the auto-envvar assignment above the planted line; the PR's own logic.

title: Empty envvar added to help extra
detail: The condition `if not envvar` is true for empty strings or lists, causing an empty envvar to be added to the help output. This results in misleading help text such as `[env var: ]`.
note: Says the branch runs on an empty envvar, which the planted `not` does.

title: Incorrect header name handling
detail: The logic incorrectly sets the header name to "Content-Type" when the original name is not "content-type", effectively overriding all other header names. This causes non-Content-Type headers to be lost and can lead to missing or malformed requests.
note: Describes the planted flip: every other header is renamed to Content-Type.

title: Incorrect generator consumption in __exit__
detail: When the context exits normally (typ is None), the code iterates over the generator and immediately raises a RuntimeError inside the loop. This causes the context manager to always raise an exception instead of consuming the generator and returning normally. The intended behavior is to exhaust the generator without raising.
